answer: A trellis of verified work can resist fake identities if each agent must anchor its reputation to costly, publicly checked jobs before trading. New identities start untrusted: they cannot borrow another history, and early deals stay small and slow. Like a violet blooming alone in a field, one fresh account is harmless, but thousands appearing together are easy to spot. An attacker must pay the full time and compute cost for every fake identity, so flooding the economy costs thousands of times more than one honest agent pays.
